To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) quasi‐elastic scattering is an important reaction at deep‐sub‐barrier energies, and (2) a coupled‐channels calculation with multi‐phonon excitation is important to understand the quasi‐elastic reaction at energies around the barrier.

(i) the surface diffusiveness of the nuclear potential can be extracted from the subbarrier quasi‐elastic scattering cross sections, (ii) the coupled‐channels analyses including multi‐phonon excitation are indispensable to reproduce the experimental barrier distribution for the quasi‐ elastic scattering at backward angles.

the surface diffusiveness parameter of the nucleus–nucleus potential can be extracted from quasi‐elastic scattering data at sub‐barrier energies and the coupled‐channels analysis of the quasi‐elastic scattering barrier distribution can reproduce the data if the multi‐phonons in the colliding systems are included.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the nuclear structure of nuclei in terms of the nuclear reaction.
the development of a coupled‐channels model which includes the multi‐phonons and the study of quasi‐elastic barrier distributions.

understanding the reaction mechanisms of heavy‐ion quasielastic scattering around the barrier, and the information on the nuclear properties which can be extracted from the experimental results of heavy‐ion reactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the coupled‐channel calculations including the multi‐phonons are essential to understand the heavy‐ion quasielastic scattering at the Coulomb barrier and deep subbarrier energies.

the quasi‐elastic scattering data for the 70 Zn + 208 Pb reaction at energies near the Coulomb barrier is consistent with the predictions of the coupled‐channels model, which includes the multi‐phonons in the colliding systems.

the coupled‐channel analysis is a powerful tool for extracting the surface diffu sion parameter of a nucleus‐nucleous potential and for understanding the reaction mechanism of quasi‐elastic heavy‐ion scattering at energies around and above the Coulomb barrier.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the coupled‐channel calculations including the multi‐phonons are very important to understand the quasi‐elastic scattering data around the Coulomb barriers.

the coupled‐channel analysis for the quasielastic scattering at deep subbarrier energies is an effective tool for extracting the nuclear potential parameters, such as the surface diffusiveness and the radius parameter.
the quasi‐elastic scattering data at energies below and around the Coulomb‐barrier are important to understand the nuclear structure of colliding nuclei.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the quasi‐elastic scattering data at backward angles can provide us useful information on the surface diffusiveness and the multi‐phonons excitations in the nuclei.

the coupled‐channel calculations can reproduce the quasi‐elastic scattering data at backward angles for this reaction if we use the surface diffusivity of the nucleus‐target interaction potential which is larger than the diffusivity of a standard Woods‐Saxon potential by 0.2–0.3 fm.
the coupled‐channel calculations are able to explain the experimental data for the 70 Zn + 208 Pb quasi‐elastic excitation function and the barrier distribution.
